queue = deque([source])

The bug: visited set is updated when node is dequeued, not when enqueued. This can cause multiple enqueues of same node, leading to longer distances? In example graph: adj = [[1,2],[2],[]], source 0. Actually seen currently {0,1}. 2 not in seen, so distance[2] = distance[1]+1 = 2 (overwrites previous 1), enqueue 2 again. Then later pop 2 (first enqueued) distance[2] currently 2? Actually after overwriting, distance[2]=2. Then pop second 2 maybe but seen already contains 2 after first pop? Actually when first 2 popped, seen adds 2, then its neighbors none. So final distance[2]=2. So bug due to visited-on-dequeue.

Thus the misconception is "Vertices marked when dequeued". The taxonomy id: graph.visited-on-dequeue.
